questions.question: Which specific laboratory finding definitively distinguishes Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) from Complement-Mediated Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (CM-HUS) in this patient, and what is the threshold value for that marker?

How does the pathophysiological role of *Capnocytophaga canimorsus* create a 'clinical paradox' regarding complement activation, and why might this organism trigger TMA in an otherwise immunocompetent adult?

Why was the initial diagnosis of autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) incorrect despite a positive Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT), and what peripheral blood smear finding provided the critical pivot toward a diagnosis of Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA)?

In the management of infection-triggered CM-HUS, what is the specific rationale for administering meningococcal vaccines and antibiotic prophylaxis prior to or concurrently with eculizumab initiation, and which bacterial genera are specifically implicated in this precaution?

Despite normal serum C3 and C4 levels, why did this patient meet the criteria for CM-HUS rather than Secondary TMA due to Sepsis/DIC alone? What specific clinical timeline and histological features supported the diagnosis of CM-HUS over pure sepsis-induced coagulopathy?

What are the distinct roles of Plasma Exchange (PEX) versus Eculizumab in the treatment algorithm for CM-HUS, and why did sustained hematologic remission fail to occur until complement blockade was established in this case?
